newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close up as political crisis eases.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close up as political crisis eases.

text.p: Italian shares closed higher on Wednesday reflecting relief that a compromise solution appears to have been reached over the Albanian crisis which had threatened to bring down Romano Prodi's centre-left government.

Prodi is now relying on the main centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance to support Italy's leadership of a mission to Albania on the basis of an agreed joint resolution that now looks certain to be approved in a vote scheduled in the lower chamber of parliament later today at around 1800 GMT.
The MIB30 blue chip index ended up 1.42 percent at 17,881 and the all-share Mibtel index 1.33 percent firmer at 12,078.
"As suspected, a compromise solution appears to have been reached which will allow Prodi's government to continue," said one share dealer.

The government faced problems after a key ally, the Communist Refoundation, refused to support the Albanian mission, but it soon become clear that the Communists were reluctant to bring the government down over the issue, dealers said.

Most blue chips gained in the market rise which largely ignored a lower start to Wall Street this afternoon, with energy giant ENI ended up 1.95 percent at 8,298 lire and industrial group Fiat 1.61 percent firmer at 5,491 lire.

Insurance group INA ended up 1.17 percent at 2,331 lire after it said late yesterday it would take a one percent stake in banking group San Paolo which closed 3.03 percent firmer at 11,374 lire. IMI ended up 0.49 percent at 15,097 lire after it said it was interested in raising its stake in San Paolo.
